drills.q: AWS engineer asks 'where are the NACLs?' Answer and translate the model.
drills.a: No per-subnet NACLs: firewall rules live at VPC level, stateful, priority-ordered, targeting tags/service accounts. Scoping = target tag (destination) + source range/tag. Implied deny-ingress at 65534.

drills.q: Service project deployer gets PERMISSION_DENIED naming a subnet. Fix?
drills.a: Grant roles/compute.networkUser on the host-project subnet to the deploying principal; for GKE also cluster SA + node SAs. Service-project IAM alone cannot fix host-side subnet access.

drills.q: You need CDN + single global IP but someone reserved Standard-tier IPs. What now?
drills.a: Global LBs/CDN require Premium tier; IPs are tier-locked so re-reserve Premium IPs, plan DNS cutover (low TTL), keep old rule during convergence (~7 days) before release.

drills.q: Design WAF rollout for a new public API with zero false-positive tolerance.
drills.a: Attach backend Armor policy; enable preconfigured OWASP sets in PREVIEW mode; analyze logged matches for legit traffic; sensitize overbroad signatures; enforce gradually per path; add rate limiting keys (IP+API key); Adaptive Protection alerts first, enforcement later.

drills.q: Three VPCs need full mesh connectivity as they grow. Peering or what?
drills.a: Peering is non-transitive -> mesh grows O(n^2). Move to Network Connectivity Center hub-and-spoke for transitive routing, or consolidate into Shared VPC when IAM centralization is acceptable.

drills.q: VM without external IP must download from storage.googleapis.com AND reach private Cloud SQL. Which features?
drills.a: Private Google Access for the API call (no external IP needed); Private Service Access range peered for Cloud SQL private IP. Independent - enable both.

drills.q: 800Mbps steady hybrid link today, 5Gbps in 18 months, no colo presence. Plan?
drills.a: Partner Interconnect ~1-2Gbps redundant now; HA VPN as encrypted backup; revisit Dedicated circuits when colo + sustained multi-Gbps justify fixed cost. BGP via Cloud Router throughout.

drills.q: L7 DDoS from residential proxies with valid TLS and headers. What still works?
drills.a: Behavioral layer: Adaptive Protection anomaly detection, rate-based bans on session/token keys, reCAPTCHA Enterprise bot scores, cache-first for anonymous GETs, per-account limits. IP/rate signatures alone insufficient - acknowledge business-layer dimension.

drills.q: Why do GKE secondary ranges need CIDR planning before first node pool?
drills.a: Pods/services draw alias IPs from immutable-range choices made early; undersized /20 pods range caps nodes x max-pods-per-node. VPC-native addressing makes pods firewall-visible - plan /16-ish for pods on big clusters (~).

drills.q: Attack hits a TCP passthrough NLB endpoint. Does Cloud Armor OWASP apply? Explain.
drills.a: No - L7 Armor rides proxy LBs only. Passthrough endpoints get inherent L3/L4 volumetric absorption plus advanced network DDoS protection under Enterprise enrollment. Policy-type-to-endpoint mapping is the tested detail.
